claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-05-26 reports: The World Bank says N’Djamena, at the Chari–Logone confluence, faces high flood risk from intense rains, rapid urban growth, clogged drains and limited emergency capacity; risk heightened after the 2022 floods and ahead of the 2024 rainy season.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-05-26 reports: The World Bank reports that 2024 PILIER works cleared and repaired 350 km of N’Djamena drains, deployed 12 pumps, trained about 30 technicians, and provided neighborhood maps and pre-positioned supplies benefiting 9,858 households; the city remained largely unharmed during high river levels.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Publisher-reported 2024 outputs and city-level result; no counterfactual evidence of losses prevented.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-02-09 reports: Citing OCHA, UNICEF says access restrictions prevented assessment or aid during displacement events in Logone Occidental, Ouaddaï and Mayo Kebbi Ouest; armed groups remained active on Lake Chad islands.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Historical OCHA-attributed access restrictions during displacement, not proof that floods caused insecurity or that a named adaptation operation was blocked.

executive_assessment.text: Eight named provinces have dated August 2026 vegetation concerns, while southern and Lac farming also faced separately reported insecurity constraints.
N'Djamena's reported drainage, pumping and preparedness outputs add concrete capacity. Historical flood and access findings are not combined into an unsupported causal chain.
